extensions.scope: The whole site: tokens on :root (light) and .dark (dark) in src/app/global.css as --home-*, mapped onto Fumadocs colours; header, theme switch, planet header, notices, the sidebar's planet row and orbit stations, the trajectory and Horizon footer in src/app/site.css; home sections and the 404 in src/app/(home)/home.css; planet and moon marks drawn by src/components/planet.tsx. Docs pages use the Fumadocs notebook layout under the shared header.

body.purpose: Base reading text and section ledes.

search-input.purpose: The hero search button text; 16px under 860px.

motion.name: home-ease
motion.purpose: The single ease for every transition on the page.

motion.purpose: The one authored, continuous moment; paused off-screen, static under reduced motion.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Section parts entering; only after scripts run; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: rail-draw

motion.name: theme-phase
motion.purpose: The theme switch planet: shadow sweep and ring tilt; instant under reduced motion.

breakpoints.purpose: At or below: one column, header nav, keyboard hints and map legend hidden.

narrative.overview:
The site is one small solar system, calm graphite space with one moving part. The star is the maker, Puncoz Nepal. Each ecosystem is an orbit; a package is a solid planet in its ecosystem's colour, its night side shaded away from the star; a project is a ringed planet. Each documented version line is a moon: full for the latest release, a crescent for an older one, a dashed new moon for `dev`. A planet's day side is Use, its night side Maintain. The home page's hero is the system itself, turning slowly beside the headline and the large search button; every later surface (cards, the planet header, the sidebar, the notices, the footer, the 404) reuses the same marks without explaining them again.

The surface is cool, technical and quiet: near-black graphite (dark is the default theme) or cool paper in light, hairline borders, one teal accent, a warm star, and colour reserved for the ecosystems. Density is moderate: generous section gaps, tight facts inside a card. Depth is soft and rare; only things that float (the search button, windows, the tooltip) lift off the ground.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite neutrals with a single signal-teal accent and a warm star; ecosystem hues mark shapes, never text.
Three faces with fixed jobs: Bricolage Grotesque for display, Onest for reading and controls, JetBrains Mono for data only.
One metaphor carrying real data: planets are entries, moons are version lines, sides are tracks.
One authored motion moment, the turning system; everything else is a short, single response.
Every state readable without scripts and without motion.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent. If something needs to stand out and it is not focus, the latest release, the current page, the lit face or a forward link, it gets weight or size, not colour. The star is light, not an accent: it lights things and is never a control's colour.

rules.name: The Shapes, Not Words Rule
rules.body: Ecosystem hues fill planets, moons and strokes. Text beside them is always Frost Ink, Steel Muted or Steel Faint, and every coloured mark has a text equivalent (the planet's name and kind, a legend label, or the card that restates the system).

rules.name: The Token-Only Surface Rule
rules.body: The browser's own surfaces (selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring), the SVG marks and the canvas read their colours from the tokens; the canvas re-reads them when the theme changes.

rules.name: The Data Voice Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for package names, versions, URLs, commands, code and counts, nothing else. Headings, buttons with words on them and prose stay in Onest or Bricolage.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline faces track negative (-0.04em to -0.01em, never tighter than -0.04em) and balance their lines; text faces keep default tracking.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only if it sits over something or frames a window. Cards lift 2px on hover by transform, not by shadow.

rules.name: The Mark Means Rule
rules.body: A ring means project, a full moon the latest release, a crescent an older release, a dashed new moon `dev`, a lock private. Never use any of them for decoration.

rules.name: The One Orbit Rule
rules.body: The system is the only continuous motion. New motion is a single, short response to arrival or input, never a second loop.

rules.name: The Visible-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content is hidden for an entrance only after scripts run; with no scripts or with reduced motion, everything is already in place.

dos: Do take every colour from the `--home-*` tokens, in both themes, including canvas strokes, SVG marks, selection, caret, scrollbar and focus.
Do keep text on Frost Ink, Steel Muted or Steel Faint; check new pairs against Graphite Ground and Graphite Panel at 4.5:1 or more.
Do draw planets, moons, suns, locks and phases from `src/components/planet.tsx` or as inline SVG; give each a text equivalent.
Do use the marks with their one meaning on every page: ring for project, full moon for latest, crescent for older, dashed new moon for `dev`, sun for Use, moon for Maintain.
Do use JetBrains Mono for package names, versions, URLs, commands, code and counts, with tabular numerals.
Do ship a reduced-motion state and a no-script state with every new animation.
donts: Don't set text in an ecosystem colour or the star colour, or let colour alone distinguish an ecosystem.
Don't add a second accent or a second continuous animation.
Don't use emoji or text glyphs as icons; draw the mark.
Don't put a shadow on a surface that does not float or frame a window.
Don't use monospace for headings, prose or button labels.
